description:
Own the checker policy's `exceptions` list in quality/comment-policy.json (R1 in the delivery plan). It is the register that lets the checker, once enforcement is blocking, accept the machine directives and required notices that must stay in source. Today the scope policy (quality/comment-cleanup-scope.json) and the checker policy hold two registers with different schemas and no cross-check; reconcile them so there is one source of truth for each retained item and a check that the two agree.

Work: register the retained directive comments (about 1,100 `# noqa`, `# type: ignore` and similar Python comments, plus the 41 suppressions that do not match the directive grammar) with their consumer, necessity and removal trigger, using shared necessity text per directive class where the justification is identical (decision D7); resolve the expiry handling so that an expired suppression date is a reported finding and never a configuration failure that exits 2 for every pull request; register the required notices and genuine parsed fixtures. Retained directive identities must be registered before candidate strict checks claim their scopes pass. Reconcile the register on the same integration branch; validate it with final whole-scope evidence before enabling the blocking candidate policy in the one final PR.

quality/comment-policy.json is a soundness-manifest path: an external review (codex, muse or agy) with a `Soundness review:` section and the repository owner's manual merge are required.
